messages.subject: Lattice layout behavior for facet_wrap
parts:
When you supply Lattice's "layout" argument with a row, column vector
whose product will result in panel layout that's smaller than the
number of panels the factors you're conditioning on will generate,
Lattice will render n pages of that layout for you. For example, if
I the conditioning I give would generate 48 panels, but I supply the
layout a vector c(4,4), lattice will generate 3 screens in
succession. Is there anyway to get facet_wrap to behave in a similar
manner?

Thanks,

Paul

messages.subject: Re: Lattice layout behavior for facet_wrap

On Sep 5, 2:00 am, paulie p <pjpug...@earthlink.net> wrote:
> When you supply Lattice's "layout" argument with a row, column vector
> whose product will result in panel layout that's smaller than the
> number of panels the factors you're conditioning on will generate,
> Lattice will render n pages of that layout for you.   For example, if
> I the conditioning I give would generate 48 panels, but I supply the
> layout a vector c(4,4), lattice will generate 3 screens in
> succession.   Is there anyway to get facet_wrap to behave in a similar
> manner?

I don't know of a short way to do this, but here is a poor man's
solution based on "for", %+% and subset():


# Turning on plot history:
windows(record = TRUE)

# A plot facetting on clarity only:
p <- qplot(carat, ..density.., data = diamonds,
geom = "histogram", binwidth = 0.2) + facet_wrap(~clarity)

# Print the plot, subsetting data to each level of `cut` in turn:
for (i in levels(diamonds$cut)) {
print(p %+% subset(diamonds, cut == i))
}

(The %+% operator specifies a new data frame for the plot.)

This is limited to putting each level of `clarity` on a separate page,
and assumes that `cut` is a factor. For a string or integer you could
use:
for (i in unique(diamonds$cut))
To convert a continuous variable to a factor, see ?cut and ?
lattice::equal.count.

Hope this helps,
Jon Olav
